newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Moderate tremor shakes Guatemala City.
newsitem.headline: Moderate tremor shakes Guatemala City.

text.p: A moderate earthquake shook Guatemala City and towns along the country's Pacific coast on Friday but caused no reported casualties or damages, officials said.

The earthquake, which measured 5.2 on the Richter scale, occurred at 8:01 a.m. (1401 GMT) and its epicentre was 68 miles (114 kms) south of Guatemala in the Pacific Ocean, Eddy Sanchez, director of the National Seismology Institute told reporters.
"At this time we have no reports of damage," Sanchez said.
He said it was the eighth earthquake felt in Guatemala this year and was the result of the Cocos tectonic plate colliding against the Continental plate.
Earlier on Friday, a 5.8 intensity earthquake hit Nicaragua, also causing no reported damage or casualties.
Guatemala has a long history of earthquakes. A major 1976 quake left 22,000 dead and one million homeless and partially destroyed Guatemala City.
